## Correct calls and misses

The 1H conversion rate collapsed from 80% (BTC) / 54% (ETH) in 2017-2018
to **27% on both coins** in 2019. Daily accuracy is still 63-70%, so the
weekly→daily layers are working — the leak is at the 4H/1H trigger layer
in a re-accumulation regime that chops harder than a trending bull or
trending bear.

The clearest signal in the entry log is **clusters of consecutive
same-direction weekly entries inside the same impulse**:

| Coin | Cluster of long entries     | Outcomes                          |
| ---- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| BTC  | 04-01, 04-08, 04-15         | correct, **incorrect**, **incorrect** |
| BTC  | 05-20, 05-27                | unresolved, **incorrect**         |
| ETH  | 04-01, 04-08, 04-15         | correct, **incorrect**, **incorrect** |
| ETH  | 05-20, 05-27                | **incorrect**, **incorrect**      |

And clusters of consecutive shorts:

| Coin | Cluster of short entries | Outcomes                  |
| ---- | ------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| BTC  | 09-30, 10-07             | **incorrect**, **incorrect** |
| BTC  | 11-25, 12-02             | **incorrect**, correct    |
| ETH  | 09-30, 10-07             | **incorrect**, **incorrect** |
| ETH  | 11-25, 12-16             | **incorrect**, correct    |

In every cluster, **the first entry was the only one with a real edge**.
The second and third entries were chasing into a more extended price
inside the same impulse leg, and they got stopped when the pullback
finally came. The system was generating "one entry per week" mechanically
regardless of whether a previous entry was still active in that
direction. The current `theory_backtest.py` walks weeks independently
with no memory of prior entries — that is the engine bug, but it is
*allowed* by the theory because the theory does not say "one entry per
zone".

## What changed and why

**One concrete theory improvement:** added
`top_down_timeframe_execution.pipeline.one_hour.re_entry_discipline`
to `docs/technical.yaml`. The new section specifies a strict rule:

> One active entry per 4H confluence zone touch. After a setup in
> direction D has been entered, no new entry in direction D until BOTH
> (a) price has traded back to a counter-direction confluence zone and
> (b) a new 4H structural element has formed at a NEW confluence zone.

The section includes:

- The rule itself, with explicit (a) and (b) preconditions.
- A rationale linked to the seven specific BTC/ETH clusters above.
- A `how_to_apply` block clarifying that losing AND winning entries
  both block re-entry until the counter-zone touch — neither outcome
  re-arms the direction by itself.
- A `relationship_to_existing_rules` note tying this to
  `pro_trader_mindset` (it is a stricter, testable version of "wait for
  the exact setup") and clarifying that it does NOT replace position
  sizing — it replaces the implicit "one signal per week = one trade"
  assumption.
- A `note_for_engines` block specifying that the engine must track
  per-coin / per-direction state across the iteration walk:
  `last_entry_zone[coin][direction]`, `last_entry_outcome`, and a
  `counter_zone_touched_since` flag. The default `theory_backtest.py`
  weekly walk currently does none of this — that is the engine
  implementation gap that this theory improvement formalizes.

### Why this is the right theory improvement for 2019

The dominant *trade-level* failure in 2019 (×16 stopped trades) is
caused by entries that should not have existed at all under a
pyramiding-discipline rule. Of the 16 incorrect 1H entries, at least 11
were second-or-third entries in the same direction within the same
impulse leg. The first entry of each cluster was correct or
unresolved; only after the pyramiding rule was added would the system
have skipped the doomed follow-ons.

This is **not** a fix for the 4H rejection bucket (×34) — that bucket is
the same engine heuristic problem iter 2 already addressed in theory
form. Both bugs are now documented; the engine fix lands in the
Phase 2-final `trading/` refactor, not in iteration commits.

## 4H/1H execution notes

- The first entry of every 2019 cluster was actually correct or
  unresolved. The signal-finding part of the chain works.
- The 1H SL placement (24-bar window low/high) is too tight in chop
  regimes — many SLs sit ~1-2% below entry while the daily ATR is 4-5%.
  This is an open question for iter 4+; today's improvement is the
  re-entry rule, not the SL rule.
- The 16 stopped trades cluster around April-May (failed continuation
  longs) and September-October (failed continuation shorts). Both
  match the typical re-accumulation profile: explosive moves followed
  by deep retracements that punish chasing.

## Open questions for later iterations

1. **SL placement in chop**: 24-bar 1H low is structurally too tight
   when daily volatility is high. Theory's `four_hour_sl` already says
   "below the 4H structural invalidation" — the engine just doesn't
   implement it.
2. **Range-vs-trend regime classifier**: in 2019 (a re-accumulation
   range), the entire weekly-bias premise is weaker. A regime
   classifier might tell the system to halve sizing or skip
   continuation entries entirely.
3. **Terminal-phase invalidation** (carried over from iter 2): the
   2017-12-11 BTC top-tick chase long is still un-addressed.
